subject: Confirming non-consumptive processing lanes, KMS onshore residency & prompt/response rights
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Jensen <sally.jensen@acmetech.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming non-consumptive processing lanes, KMS onshore residency & prompt/response rights

Hi Sally —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per your ask from procurement/legal, I wanted to put the operational details in writing so your team can validate against AcmeTech's DPA checklist. Below are the concrete pieces Redwood can confirm today and the items we propose as evidence/workflow to close the loop.

1) No-model-improvement (non-consumptive) processing
- Commitment: Redwood will not use customer inputs or outputs to improve or update any shared models for AcmeTech's selected tenant(s) unless an explicit opt-in/contract amendment is executed. This is scoped at tenant-level for the Dedicated/Private offerings.
- Operational proof: we can provide a runbook + short audit trace from our inference runtime showing the "learning flag" set to false for your tenant ID during a sample window.

2) Prompt & Response ownership
- Redwood acknowledges that prompts and returned responses from your tenant are treated as customer content and will not be used to assert derivative ownership over your outputs. We can provide language for the DPA and SOW that maps to your IP and output-entitlement requirements.

3) KMS residency / onshore keying
- For US-region deployments we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and can persist keys in your dedicated KMS project or our managed onshore KMS depending on the Private/Dedicated flavor.
- Evidence: KMS binding diagram, access logs for key operations, and a short matrix of which subprocessors (if any) can request key operation metadata.

Requested next steps from us:
- I can attach a short evidence pack (SOC2 summary, ops playbook, KMS diagram) for legal review.
- If Acme needs an export demonstrating the non-learning flag over a 7-day sample, we can run that and provide logs and the associated inference trace.

If you prefer, we can loop in Karthik from legal & David from Ops for a quick 30-minute call to verify the exported artifacts and the wording.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Head of Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (attachment), no-train-ops-playbook.zip (attachment), kms-residency-diagram.png (attachment)

From: Sally Jensen <sally.jensen@acmetech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: AcmeTech Legal <legal@acmetech.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Confirming non-consumptive processing lanes, KMS onshore residency & prompt/response rights

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. A few follow-ups from legal/procurement: 

- For the non-learning sample export, can you confirm the minimal fields included in the trace? Legal wants confirmation there is no user-identifying telemetry in the sample output (we can redact), and that the logs only show the learning flag and basic request metadata (timestamp, tenant id, model id).

- On prompt/response ownership: we need a short clause we can include in the DPA that says Acme retains exclusive rights to prompts and outputs and that Redwood will not claim derivatives or reuse those outputs in any models. Can you provide model language?

- For KMS: we need the list of subprocessors who may have access to key metadata (not plaintext key material). Also, are there any third-party operators (partners/cloud providers) outside the US who could have operational-level access during escalation? We require assurance that keys and key operations for our US tenant remain in US jurisdiction.

If you can attach the sample trace fields and proposed DPA clause, we can move faster. Also, can we schedule the short call tomorrow morning (9–11am ET)?

Best,
Sally
Procurement Lead — AcmeTech

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Jensen <sally.jensen@acmetech.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Confirming non-consumptive processing lanes, KMS onshore residency & prompt/response rights

Sally —

Thanks, and good asks. Attached is the evidence pack we referenced plus a proposed DPA paragraph you can drop into your redline: see the file named "DPA-proposed-clause.txt" inside the ops playbook zip. Quick answers inline below and an ask for the call.

- Sample trace fields: timestamp (UTC), tenant_id (hashed for sample), model_id, request_id, learning_flag (boolean), request_token_count. Example: {timestamp: 2026-08-15T14:01:03Z, tenant_id: <redacted-hash>, model_id: gpt-redwood-13b, request_id: r-8a9f, learning_flag: false, request_token_count: 124}
  - Note: we redact user text for the sample export; if Acme wants unredacted traces under an NDA we can discuss a controlled review.

- Proposed DPA language (excerpt): "Customer retains all rights, title and interest in and to Customer Content (including prompts, inputs and outputs). Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, improve or otherwise modify any model accessible outside the Customer’s tenant without Customer’s prior written consent." Full clause is in the attached text.

- Subprocessors & KMS access: for Private deployments where Acme brings its own KMS, Redwood operators do not have access to key material. For Redwood-managed onshore KMS we list the subprocessors that may interact with KMS operation metadata (operations vendor, primary cloud provider US region). Those subprocessors are named in the SOC2 appendix in the evidence pack. No international support partners have direct access to KMS ops for US-resident keys; escalation runbooks route to US-based on-call only.

Call availability: Karthik and David are available tomorrow 10:30–11:00am ET. Does that work for you and AcmeTech legal?

Regards,
Soojin

Attachments: DPA-proposed-clause.txt (inside no-train-ops-playbook.zip), SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf, kms-residency-diagram.png

Subject: Internal: AcmeTech evidence & next steps

Quick internal note after our call today — thanks all for joining. Summary and action items: 

- Acme legal asked explicitly for the sample export fields and the DPA clause (we delivered both in the pack). Good to have an internal copy of the unredacted run to support legal if they request.
- Ops (David) to prepare a 7-day non-learning audit export (redacted by default) and retain an unredacted copy in a gated location; deliver redacted to Acme by EOD Monday.
- Karthik to confirm subprocessors list and add the onshore-only escalation statement to the DPA clause.
- Pricing note: Acme will likely request an additional compliance fee for dedicated onshore KMS ops — sales to propose increment in the next SOW.

I'll shepherd the assets into the deal record. Soojin: please confirm EOD Monday delivery for the redacted export and ping me to attach to the HubSpot ticket.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
